title_as_printed:
Measured bubble pressure

for salt solutions of molality m

footnotes_as_printed.a: Values for m = 3.000 mol/kg and 1.000 mol/kg of NaCl were taken from reference 2.
footnotes_as_printed.b: When no value of dp is tabulated, only the pressure p_d for bubble appearance could be measured.

pressure_note: = (p_a + p_d)/2, mean of pressures of bubble appearance (decreasing p) and disappearance (increasing p); dp = (p_a - p_d)/2 (as stated in the text); this is the solution bubble (vapour) pressure

uncertainty.what: half-difference of the two pressure readings, not an accuracy

skip_rows.reason: salt label rows KCl, NaCl, CaCl2

conversion_needs: the salt of each row comes from the preceding label row; 'm mol/kg' is the molality of that salt
notes: Printed as two side-by-side column groups: KCl (left) and NaCl (right); the CaCl2 section uses both groups (left group T about 623 K, right group 623.02 K then 642.8 K). Stacked left group then right group per section. Footnote a is printed on the m cell of the first two KCl rows (3.0000) and on NaCl rows 3.000 and 1.000, although its text refers to NaCl values only; kept as printed in the note column. Footnote b stands alone in the dp cell of two CaCl2 rows (cell written empty, note 'dp MPa:b'). Printed dp 0.00 kept. Table 2 supplies the same solutions' densities.

row_from_literature.reason: footnote a: NaCl values at m=3.000 and 1.000 taken from the authors earlier paper (ref. 2, Crovetto and Wood 1991), not new measurements
footnote letter a is also printed on the first two KCl 3.0000 rows although the footnote names NaCl; held conservatively (mapping audit 2026-10-02)
